behavioral_notes.observation: hr_timesheet does NOT define its own timesheet model: it _inherit = 'account.analytic.line' (models/hr_timesheet.py) and adds task_id/project_id/employee_id. A timesheet IS literally an analytic cost line — this is the structural bridge that lets a support activity (HR labour) be posted onto the value-shop's analytic account (the project). Not visible in metadata as the model name is reused.

On create/write, when unit_amount/employee_id/account_id change, the analytic line's monetary `amount` is recomputed as amount = -unit_amount * cost, where cost = employee_id.hourly_cost (via _hourly_cost(), from the hr_hourly_cost dependency), then currency-converted to the analytic account currency. This is the support->primary cost computation: logged hours become a signed cost on the project's analytic account. Formula lives in Python, not metadata.

effective_hours rolls up via _read_group on timesheet_ids.unit_amount:sum onto each task; subtask_effective_hours recurses over child_ids; progress = (effective+subtask)/allocated_hours, overtime = max(total-allocated,0), remaining_hours = allocated - spent. The delivered effort of the shop is measured here; these stored computes are the task-level KPIs metadata cannot show.

project.project.create auto-creates an account.analytic.account when allow_timesheets is set and none is provided (and _check_allow_timesheet raises if timesheets are on without an analytic account). The analytic account is the 'vessel' of the value-shop into which support costs and primary revenue converge; the module enforces its existence.

classification.rationale: hr_timesheet measures and costs the delivered effort of the value-shop: it _inherit's account.analytic.line so a logged hour IS an analytic cost line posted onto the project's analytic account (the engagement's value vessel), priced via employee.hourly_cost (hr_hourly_cost). It is the execution/control activity of the shop — the bridge that makes consulting/services billable (consumed downstream by sale_timesheet) and lets profit-per-engagement be computed by comparing accumulated support costs (labour, expenses, purchases) against primary revenue on the same analytic account. The depends (hr, hr_hourly_cost, analytic, project) wire this support->primary integration. Activity is primary because it is the engagement's effort-execution and cost-control loop, not back-office enablement.

automatic labour costing: amount = -hours x employee hourly_cost, currency-converted to the analytic account
